answer: Rotating Entry Inlet. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon assigns agents to shards; only the inlet of a randomly drawn shard may admit new identities that epoch. An attacker cannot precompute which shard or when, so it must sustain live presence across all shards, paying compute and bandwidth for every dune of dormant capacity it keeps ready. A nebula of fake identities earns nothing until its shard is drawn, and wasted readiness cost compounds per epoch.
